title: oneisall Automatic Cat Feeder for 2 Cats, 20 Cups/5L Automatic Cat Food Dispenser for Small Pets Indoor, Timed Cat Feeder for Dry Food

reviews.title: PERFECTO
reviews.body: Lo compre para despreocuparme de los horarios de la comida de mis perros.Ahora esta perfecto, recibe su comida 3 veces al día y funciona a la perfección.Me hubiera gustado que fuera de pila recargable, ya que el producto tiene que estar 100% conectado al enchufe todo el tiempo para su funcionalidad o en otro caso se le ponen pilas 🔋

reviews.title: Set and Forget!
reviews.body: Great feeder overall! I picked this up in case I eventually get two cats, and it works well for that purpose. One thing to note: there’s no option to feed just one side—both sides dispense food at the same time. So if you’re only feeding one cat, you’ll need to halve the portions to avoid overfeeding.The portion sizes are preset (ranging from 1/16 cup to 1 cup) and can’t be customized beyond that, but it’s been sufficient for my needs. I specifically wanted a feeder with a large hopper, and the metal trays are a nice bonus. It also feels very secure and cat-proof, so clever cats won’t be able to sneak extra food.
reviews.author: A Canadian Shopper

reviews.title: très utile
reviews.body: Cela fait un mois qu'il est en fonction et tout va bien. Au début, j'ai un peu surdosé car il est possible de mettre 36 doses mais 18 doses remplissent déjà bien les gamelles. Pour mes chats 4 doses 2 fois par jour suffisent et j'ai une autonomie de plus de 3 semaines. Il est aussi difficile de retirer les gamelles en inox et j'ai ajouté un tout petit bout de ruban adhesif pour le faire plus facilement. Sinon, c'est un très bon appareil. Attention, la prise du petit trasfo n'est pas EU. Un transfo de base suffit car le cable est USB.
reviews.author: Antoine F.

reviews.title: Do you have raccoons?
reviews.body: I REALLY like this feeder!  It is the first auto feeder I have purchased.  We live in the country and found a momma cat and 4 kittens on our front porch recently.  She was pretty frail, so we started putting food out for her and the kittens and it was well received.We were going to be traveling for a week, so I went looking for a feeder.  I consciously had raccoons on the brain when I was shopping.  I was looking for one with a shape that I could have a shot at somehow securing.  This one has a nice flat top and I envisioned being able to place something heavy'ish on it.  I was right.  I imagined that I would have a decent chance of beating the raccoons.  I was wrong.The first night, I placed a small weight on it to test the waters.  Came out the next morning and found the feeder about 3 feet from where I had placed it.  It was on its side and in several pieces (not broke, just disassembled...  much of the product is held together by gravity).The next night, I placed a 16x8x2 inch concrete patio paver on top of it.  It weighed in at just over 16.5 pounds.  The feeder certainly wasn't designed with this in mind, but it held up like a champ.  The feeder was up against a wall, so the front and two sides were exposed.My greatest regret was that I placed all of this directly under my security camera, out of its line of sight.  I came out the next morning and again found it laid over and in pieces with the patio stone on the ground where the feeder previously was.  The security footage showed a raccoon come up and was evidently there for 15-20 mins then left.  A little later it came back with a friend to finish the job.We were leaving that day so I hung my head in defeat and let the neighbor take care of the cats.  I'm certain that I can up with a better challenge for the raccoons, but I haven't tried yet.To this feeder's credit though, it took a beating those two nights and survived with only a few scuffs on the face where they were evidently dragging it across the porch.  Still works perfectly.  Also to the feeder's credit, it has a VERY flexible feeding schedule which was easy to set up.  My original plan was to feed 3 or 4 times during the day and try to limit what food was left in the bowls overnight to maybe limit what was attracted to it.  That attraction portion of that sentence was just dumb thinking on my part.  The scheduling part worked perfect though.As I was putting it together the first time (super easy) I actually caught myself thinking "oh, that's a smart way to design that..."  I don't do that often.  It really is a neat design overall.  I can vouch that comes apart and cleans very easy if you find it covered in racoon drool.I was able to plug it in, but it has a nice battery backup for peace of mind.In came into this purchase knowing that I was going to be asking something of it that in no way it was advertised to do.  It met every expectation, was easy to use, holds a ton of food, is easy to clean and is very robust.  5 stars from me.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on 19 July 2024
reviews.author: J. Smith

features: Easy to Set Up: oneisall automatic cat food dispenser has a dial to simplify the programme. Everyone can easily set up it and control feeding
Peaceful Mealtime for 2 Cats: The bowls are placed opposite with an 11-inch distance. It creates a comfortable space for each cat to eat same amount of food. Avoid queuing or fighting
5 L/20 Cups Capacity: A full tank of dry food allows 2 adult cats to eat for 10 days. You don’t need to ask neighbors or pet sisters to feed your pets when you go away for weekend or vacation
10 s Voice Recorder: You can record a 10 s calling message. The feeder would play the audio before each meal
Precise Portion control: 1 Portion ≈ 10 Grams ≈ 1/12 Cup. Allowed kibble size less than 0.5 inch. Up to 6 meals a day. The portion means the kibble amount of each bowl
